target.title: fix(agents): strip C1 control characters (0x80-0x9f) in sanitizeForConsole
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sanitizeForConsole()` in `src/agents/console-sanitize.ts` filters C0 control characters (0x00-0x1f) and DEL (0x7f) but leaves the **C1 control range (0x80-0x9f)** unhandled. The C1 range includes 0x9b (CSI — Control Sequence Introducer), an alternative ANSI escape prefix equivalent to ESC [. An attacker who controls text flowing through `sanitizeForConsole` could inject C1-based ANSI escape sequences into console/log output.

The more comprehensive `sanitizeForLog` in `packages/terminal-core/src/ansi.ts` already strips both C0 and C1 ranges. This fix makes `sanitizeForConsole` consistent with that pattern for the control-character subset.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `(code >= 0x80 && code <= 0x9f)` to the control character filter condition, covering all 32 C1 bytes (0x80-0x9f) including the CSI introducer at 0x9b.

## User Impact

Console diagnostic strings containing C1 control bytes no longer leak ANSI escape sequences into terminal/log output. No impact on normal text — C1 bytes are non-printable control characters.

## Evidence

### Standalone proof (production helper, same head)

```
$ node --import tsx test/_proof_console_sanitize_c1.mjs
node=24.12.0

input: text<0x9b>[31mred
output: text[31mred
expected: text[31mred
PASS: C1 CSI stripped
C1 range 0x80-0x9f all stripped: true
```

### Tests

```
$ npx vitest run src/agents/console-sanitize.test.ts
# All tests pass including new C1 range test
```

### Files Changed (2 files, +15/-2)

```
 src/agents/console-sanitize.test.ts | 11 +++++++++++
 src/agents/console-sanitize.ts      |  6 ++++--
```
